diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $A\in\R^{d\times d}$ be skew-symmetric,  $b\in\R^{d}$, and suppose that $\pi(x)\coloneqq Ax+b$ satisfies $\pi=0$ on $\Gamma$, whereby $\pi=0$ on $H_{1}\cup H_{2}$.
\bv \mapsto \norm{\bv \cdot \bn}_{L^q(\Gamma)}\qquad \text{is a norm on the  rigid deformations $\mathcal{R}(\Omega)$}

issues.failure_explanation: The hypothesis relevant to Assumption \ref{assump:dom} is only $\pi\cdot\bn=0$, but the proof replaces it by the much stronger condition $\pi=0$. In dimension three, take two faces with normals $e_1,e_2$ and the nonzero rigid translation $\pi=e_3$; it has zero normal component on both faces. Thus two non-collinear normals do not make the normal-trace seminorm a norm.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the criterion so that the selected face normals eliminate every translation and rotation—for example, require sufficiently many spanning normals—and replace the proof by one using $\pi\cdot\bn=0$ rather than $\pi=0$.
issues.overall_effect: The stated geometric criterion and the corresponding claim in the figure discussion are false, although the full-boundary property needed later for a bounded polyhedron may be established under stronger geometric information.
issues.title: Two non-collinear face normals do not eliminate all rigid translations
issues.why_classification: The corollary needs a genuine strengthening of its geometric hypotheses and a new argument, but this is localized and need not alter the main numerical method.

issues.failure_explanation: A componentwise scalar Scott--Zhang operator does not in general commute with multiplication by the piecewise varying boundary normal, so the displayed equality used to prove normal-trace preservation is invalid. Moreover, the operator's range is the piecewise linear space, while the claimed image is all of $X_h\cap H^1_{\bn}$ even though the assumptions only require the piecewise linear space to be contained in $X_h$; for higher-order $X_h$ that equality cannot hold.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Construct a boundary-condition-preserving interpolant for the smooth test functions actually used, with the required approximation estimates, or modify the limit passage to control the residual normal trace.
issues.overall_effect: The test functions used in the limit passage are not shown to have exactly zero normal trace, so the pressure and Nitsche boundary terms cannot be discarded as claimed.
issues.title: The asserted Scott--Zhang preservation of zero normal trace is unsupported and false as stated
issues.why_classification: A contained replacement construction can plausibly preserve the convergence theorem, but the stated standard Scott--Zhang argument does not provide it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By the triangle inequality and a trace estimate, the local stability estimates follows from the approximation estimate.

issues.failure_explanation: For an affine function with nonzero constant gradient, the left side scales like $h^{(d-1)/2}$, whereas the local $H^2$ norm on a patch scales like $h^{d/2}$. Hence no mesh-independent constant can satisfy the claimed estimate. A correctly scaled local estimate needs an $h^{-1/2}\|\nabla v\|_{L^2}$ term. The global boundary estimate used later may still be proved separately by a global trace argument.

issues.failure_explanation: The estimate $\delta_k^2\sum_j\|\pi_j^k\|^p\le C$ does not control the primitive $\xi^k$: it is weaker by a factor of $\delta_k$ than an $L^p$ bound for $\pi^k$, and cumulative values can grow without cancellation. Thus the asserted weak compactness of $\xi^k$ is unsupported. It would have to be derived from the time-summed discrete equations, exploiting telescoping of the velocity increments and bounds on the remaining terms.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a separate uniform estimate for the pressure primitive by summing the discrete momentum equations in time and applying the inf-sup condition to the accumulated equation.
issues.overall_effect: The pressure limit used with non-discretely-divergence-free interpolated test functions is not established, leaving the limiting weak equation and both main convergence proofs incomplete.
issues.title: The accumulated pressure bound does not follow from the discrete pressure estimate
issues.why_classification: A new but contained pressure-primitive estimate is needed; it does not require changing the scheme or the advertised convergence regime.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: While in space we have full admissibility, in time some integrability is missing due to the convective term.

Due to the convective term, the velocity function is not an admissible test function for the three dimensional time-dependent Navier--Stokes equations. 
	For this reason, only an energy inequality rather than an equality is available.

From the exponents we see that admissibility of 
a solution as test function 
is lost in dimension $d = 3$.

issues.failure_explanation: The established three-dimensional regularity is only $u\in L^\infty(I;L^2)\cap L^2(I;H^1)$ with the corresponding low time integrability of the convective term. The paper itself notes that this does not make $u$ an admissible test function. The brief mollification assertion does not supply the missing limit for the nonlinear term, so it cannot upgrade the usual energy inequality to equality.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either establish additional regularity sufficient for energy equality or replace the $r>2$ identification by a new argument compatible with only an energy inequality.
issues.overall_effect: The energy identity in the proposition is unsupported in dimension three. More importantly, the Minty limsup argument for $r>2$ uses that identity, so the antisymmetric-method convergence theorem is not proved in the advertised three-dimensional range $2<r<4$.
issues.title: Energy equality is claimed at three-dimensional Leray regularity
issues.why_classification: Repairing the three-dimensional $r>2$ theorem requires new proof architecture or abandoning an advertised exponent and dimension regime.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that $\bv \mapsto \mu(\abs{\bv}) \frac{\bv}{\abs{\bv}} + \lambda \bv$ for $\lambda = \beta(a - b)$ is monotone;

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed $\Seps$ regularizes the physical decreasing-friction map itself. Along a ray its scalar magnitude is $\mu(t)t/\sqrt{\varepsilon^2+t^2}$, whose derivative is negative away from the tiny regularization region for the stated decreasing $\mu$ and small $\varepsilon$. Thus $\Seps$ is not monotone and does not satisfy the regularisation assumption. It is the shifted map $\Seps+\lambda\,\mathrm{Id}$ that could serve as the monotone approximation, with $-\lambda u_\tau$ then restored separately.

failure_location.quote: regularising this as above yields that $\Seps$ satisfies Assumption~\ref{assump:gbd-reg} (see Example \ref{ex:reg-rel}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State and use the shifted monotone regularisation $\widehat{\Seps}=\Seps+\lambda\,\mathrm{Id}$ in the analytical decomposition, subtracting $\lambda u_\tau$ in the physical stress.
issues.overall_effect: The stated link between this numerical regularisation and the analytical regularisation framework is false, though the experiment itself can still be interpreted as solving the regularized nonmonotone law.
issues.title: The numerical nonmonotone regularisation is not monotone as claimed
issues.why_classification: A short local correction to the shifted/unshifted notation restores the intended decomposition without changing the computed physical boundary term.
